clusters.label: Mechanical stability
clusters.definition: Stability of a crystal against mechanical deformation, assessed theoretically through elastic properties and, where specified, Born stability criteria.
clusters.reason: The evidence consistently denotes theoretically assessed mechanical stability of crystalline solids. Compositions, phases, strains, pressures, comparative stability and supporting indicators remain claim-specific; none changes the concept into dynamical or thermodynamic stability or a stability reduction.

unresolved.reason: Temperature sensitivity is asserted alongside thermoelectric performance, but the response variable and sensitivity definition are unspecified; cross-paper equivalence cannot be established.
The supplied Seebeck coefficient characterizes thermoelectric performance, while temperature sensitivity is separately asserted without a definition or response variable.

clusters.label: Open-circuit voltage
clusters.definition: Electrical potential difference across a device's terminals under open-circuit conditions.
clusters.reason: Both denote the same terminal voltage quantity. Different electrolyte and film contexts, and their temperature-response relations, do not redefine open-circuit voltage as a particular thermopower subtype.

clusters.label: Durability during repeated stretching
clusters.definition: Ability of a material to withstand repeated stretching while retaining performance.
clusters.reason: Both explicitly concern durability under repeated stretching. The first specifies thermopower retention after 1000 cycles; its liquid-nitrogen result separately supports freezing resistance. Material identities and quantitative cycling results remain claim-specific.
